ov: A wild camelid of South America and the ancestor of the domestic llama. It is one of the largest land mammals native to South America today, with a light brown to cinnamon coat, a white belly and a grey face. It is a fast runner and an excellent swimmer.
rg: Peru, Bolivia, Chile and Argentina, especially Patagonia, with a few in Paraguay; a small introduced herd lives in the Falklands.

cf.tip: The llama is the domesticated descendant of the guanaco; the guanaco’s colour varies very little.

fx: It runs at up to 56 km/h, often over steep, rocky ground.
Some live in the Atacama Desert, where parts have had no rain for over 50 years.
